q: Le Corbusier is the pen name of which architect?
n: Le Corbusier was born Charles-Édouard Jeanneret in Switzerland; Pierre Jeanneret was his cousin and partner.

q: Which chair did Marcel Breuer design at the Bauhaus?
n: Breuer's bent steel-tube Wassily Chair (1925) was named for Kandinsky; the Barcelona Chair is Mies's, the Paimio Aalto's, the LC4 Le Corbusier's.

q: Which of Le Corbusier's Five Points lifts the building off the ground?
n: Le Corbusier's Five Points (1926): pilotis, free plan, free façade, horizontal ribbon windows and roof garden.

q: Which New York museum did Marcel Breuer design (1966)?
n: Breuer's granite, stepped-out Whitney on Madison Avenue opened in 1966; the Guggenheim is Wright's.

q: Which Potsdam observatory tower did Erich Mendelsohn design?
n: The Einstein Tower (1921) is the best-known work of German Expressionism; it housed a solar telescope.

q: Which architect is often called the "father of skyscrapers"?
n: Sullivan gave the tall steel-framed office building its form (Wainwright Building, 1891); Wright was his apprentice.

q: Which house did Philip Johnson build for himself in New Canaan, Connecticut (1949)?
n: Johnson's Glass House was inspired by Mies's Farnsworth House; Fallingwater is Wright's and Villa Savoye Le Corbusier's.

q: Which Finnish architect was the father of Eero Saarinen?
n: Eliel Saarinen designed Helsinki Central Station and later ran the Cranbrook Academy, where his son Eero trained.

q: Mies van der Rohe was the last director of which school, before it closed in 1933?
n: Mies led the Bauhaus from 1930 until the Nazis forced it to close in 1933; he then moved to Chicago (IIT).

q: Which building did Walter Gropius design for his school in Dessau (1925–26)?
n: When the Bauhaus moved from Weimar to Dessau, Gropius designed its glass-walled workshop wing and school.

q: Which of Le Corbusier's Five Points lets interior walls go anywhere because columns carry the load?
n: Le Corbusier's Five Points (1926): pilotis, free plan, free façade, horizontal ribbon windows and roof garden.

q: Which movement does Erich Mendelsohn's early work belong to?
n: Mendelsohn's sketches and the Einstein Tower show the flowing, sculptural forms of Expressionism.

q: Which glass-walled factory (1911) did Walter Gropius design with Adolf Meyer?
n: The Fagus Factory's glass corners without columns made it an early landmark of modern architecture; the AEG factory is by Behrens.

q: Which New York tower did Philip Johnson design with a "Chippendale" broken-pediment top?
n: Johnson and Burgee's AT&T Building (1984) became an icon of postmodernism; Lever House is by SOM.
